high_roi_rule.description: EXPERIMENTAL SCREEN, NOT AN ROI MODEL. Identical to the dashboard's 'Model watch' filter: category_basis == 'seed' (series in the official fee schedule) and volume_24h_fp > 0. The owner's model was not supplied (F-14).
high_roi_rule.decided_at: detection time — build_alerts.py applies this screen to the snapshot it is reading and the archive is append-only, so the flag is a record of that moment and is never relabelled later. validate_alerts.py therefore checks each flag against the volume_24h_fp / category_basis stored with the alert, and reports disagreement with the current snapshot as drift (volume_24h_fp legitimately changes between collections) instead of failing the collector — see F-39 and scripts/tests/test_alerts.py HighRoiFreezeTests.

disclaimers: Prices are last-traded prices from the Kalshi DEMO environment (mock funds).
Each alert is a change between two consecutive collector observations, not a continuous tick stream.
Alerts are kept in data/live/alerts_archive.json, so a move stays listed after its market leaves the open scan.
cause_link is null on every alert: no official cause source has been collected, so none is shown.
high_roi is the dashboard's experimental 'Model watch' screen (seed series with positive volume_24h). It is not an owner-approved ROI model.

Category integrity: an archived alert is withheld from both feeds (counts.withheld_category_conflict) when the market's own snapshot row records official series categories that exclude it from that topic. The archive itself is never rewritten.
